# IGRM Weekly Assessment: Week ending 6 August 2026

## Executive assessment

Aggregate press salience moderated over the week without normalising. The seven-day composite ended at 61.5, against 67.5 on 30 July, a decline of 6.0 points. The daily composite fell more sharply, from 70.0 to 48.9, and all five daily channel readings were lower on the point-to-point comparison.

For a weekly assessment, the seven-day measures provide the more representative signal. Attention remained concentrated in the western-border, maritime and Gulf channels, each of which ended at the 77th percentile of its own history or above. The softer composite therefore reflects a narrower distribution of attention, not its disappearance.

## Channel positioning

Pakistan/Western Border was the highest seven-day channel at 88.9, up 0.4 points. Shipping/Chokepoints declined 9.5 points to 88.5, while Gulf/Energy eased 1.2 points to 77.3. Both remained elevated relative to their own trailing histories. US/Trade recorded the largest seven-day decline, falling 30.2 points to 23.0.

China/Eastern Border rose 10.5 points on the seven-day measure to 29.9, even as its daily reading fell from 71.9 to 5.3. Intraweek spikes lifted the persistent measure while the closing observation fell sharply. This time-horizon split is the clearest reason not to treat one day's reading as a summary of the week.

## External comparator: Strait of Hormuz

Across the 393 weeks shared with IMF PortWatch, IGRM's Hormuz press-salience measure ranked at the 95.4th percentile for the latest week, while recorded transit activity ranked at the 0.4th. The resulting gap was 95.0 percentile points.

The comparison documents disagreement between two measurement systems; it does not explain the traffic count. It is not evidence of closure, a forecast of physical disruption, or an estimate of risk.

## Calibration sensitivity

Under the frozen independent-overlap re-estimation of the NGrams splice, the daily composite is 48.3 rather than 48.9, and the seven-day composite is 65.3 rather than 61.5. The aggregate interpretation, elevated weekly salience alongside a softer daily close, holds under both calibrations.

Channel-level sensitivity is more material. Pakistan/Western Border is 84.4 rather than 88.9 and China/Eastern Border is 53.4 rather than 29.9; Gulf/Energy is unchanged at 77.3. US/Trade and Shipping have no new independent overlap and remain at their production values. China is therefore the channel most affected by calibration uncertainty, and its level should be used with that caveat.

## Monitoring statement

The next release will track whether western-border and maritime attention remains above the 80th percentile, whether China's intraweek volatility recurs, and whether the Hormuz salience-transit gap narrows in either series. These are monitoring conditions, not forecasts. IGRM measures the distribution of press attention; it does not estimate the probability or severity of geopolitical events.
